Fully Funded PhD Studentship: Natural Language Processing for Low-Resource Languages

The School of Computer Science at Northvale University invites applications for a fully funded PhD studentship in natural language processing (NLP), focusing on large language models for low-resource languages and self-supervised learning.

Project

Many of the world's languages remain low-resource. This project will develop self-supervised and multilingual methods to adapt large language models to low-resource languages, including conversational AI applications. The student will be supervised by Dr. Amara Okafor (a.okafor@cs.northvale.ac.uk) within the Language Technology Group.

Funding

The studentship covers tuition fees at the home and international rate and provides a tax-free stipend of £19,237 per annum for 3.5 years.

A research training support grant (RTSG) of £1,500 per year is also available for conference travel and research costs.

Eligibility

Applicants should hold, or expect to obtain, a Master's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence or a related discipline.

English language requirements

Applicants whose first language is not English must meet the University's English language requirement: IELTS 6.5 overall with no less than 6.0 in each component, or equivalent.

Test results can be submitted after an offer is made; successful applicants without a test will receive a conditional offer.

Applicants who have completed a degree taught in English at a recognised institution may be exempt from this requirement.

How to apply

Please submit the following documents through the online application portal:

  • Your CV (maximum 2 pages)
  • A cover letter explaining your motivation and fit for the project (max 2 pages, PDF)
  • Academic transcripts and degree certificates
  • Names and contact details of two referees
  • A research proposal (optional, up to 1,500 words)

There is no application fee for postgraduate research applications.

Application deadline

Application deadline: 15 January 2027, 23:59 GMT. Interviews are expected in the week of 8 February 2027.

Expected start date: 1 October 2027.

Apply now

For questions about the project, contact the supervisor: Dr. Amara Okafor.
